To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the propagation of macroeconomic disturbances through input output and geography networks has first order effects on the macroeconomy, and that the propagation is larger than would be predicted by the direct effects of these disturbances.

1) the propagation of macroeconomic fluctuations through input-output and geographic networks is a first-order phenomenon, and 2) the pattern of propagation is different for different types of shocks.

(i) the propagation of macroeconomic fluctuations through input-output networks is quantitatively important and can have important macroeconomic implications; (ii) the propagation is consistent with the theory that demand side shocks propagate to input supplying industries, and supply side shocks to customer industries; (iii) the propagation of shocks is quantitatively larger than the direct impact of the shock; (iv) the propagation is also important through geographic networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transmission of macroeconomic shocks and the propagation of shocks through input output networks and geographic networks.
the propagation of economic shocks through input-output and geographic networks and the implications for the macro economy.
the role of economic networks in the propagation of shocks and the implications for aggregate economic performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the propagation of economic shocks through economic networks is an important driver of macroeconomic dynamics and that the magnitude of the propagation of a shock through the network is quantitatively larger than the direct effect of the shock.
the transmission of macroeconomic shocks is an important driver of the business cycle.

our analysis of the input output network and geographic collocation of industries suggests that economic shocks propagate in a manner that is consistent with theory and that these network effects are quantitatively important.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the propagation of macroeconomic fluctuations through the input-output and geographic network of the economy can be an important driver of macroeconomic outcomes.

we have developed a framework for analyzing the propagation of shocks through the economy and we have used that framework to analyze a number of different types of shocks and to quantify their propagation through the economy.
economic networks can have important implications for the macro economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a need for a more comprehensive understanding of the propagation of economic shocks through the economy, and the role that economic networks play in that propagation, to better inform macroeconomic models and policy.
the transmission of shocks through the economy can be a very powerful driver of macroeconomy fluctuations, and that this can have important implications for the design of macroeconomic policy.
the propagation of economic shocks through economic networks can be a first order driver of macroeconomic dynamics.
